name: twolayer-ab
measures: Is a per-eye artefact of the two-layer foveated submission in what we submit or in the runtime's composition (artifacts\flash-07: white feathered disc on the right eye after the Pimax runtime of 2026-11-06)? Each arm captures 40 submissions twice (real and generated frames alternate at 2X): both projection layers, both eyes, colour AND alpha of the focus layer per array slice, the layer flags (capture.jsonl). verdict.py / compose.py: the focus layer of slice 1 (right eye) must match slice 0's statistics (alpha feather, colour not near-white where the periphery under it is not); a white disc in our submission = our bug (OFXR slice-1 synthesis), a clean submission while the headset shows the disc = the runtime. Arms: array2 = as shipped (dcsvr_two_layers=2: one array swapchain per layer, slice = eye); pereye = dcsvr_two_layers=1 (one swapchain per eye and layer: the runtime's array path is not used); fg1x = frame generation 1X with the same two layers (generated frames out of the picture). The simulated gaze keeps the focus moving the same way in every arm, with or without a tracker.
cannotJudge: What the headset shows: the capture is what reaches the runtime. Pair it with the compositor mirror (memory: Pimax compositor mirror via PVR keys; black while the headset is untracked) or the user's eye. Whether OFXR's foveated mode accepts dcsvr_two_layers=1: the pereye arm's flight log must show foveated_mode result=3 with per-eye roles, else that arm only says 'not supported'.
sideEffects: the real eye tracker is ignored (simulated gaze); dcsvr_two_layers is changed only in the flown copy's settings.cfg
40 submissions per capture at scale 2: about 0.4 GB per capture
